findings.title: Failed device tag is cached, disabling the limit
findings.body: tagDeviceUI does localCache.SetDefault(key) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and never removes it on error. When CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the caller in client.go denies auth once, but the key is now cached, so the next request from the same new device hits `if _, ok := localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }` and succeeds without touching the DB. The device limit is therefore only enforced once per device per cache lifetime (~29m) and then bypassed.

findings.title: updateDevice uses ? placeholders on all dialects
findings.body: updateDevice builds `UPDATE anon_device ... WHERE device_id = ? ...` with `?` placeholders for every database, while CreateOrUpdateDevice in the same file special-cases Postgres to use $1..$5. On Postgres the update path (the only path taken when count >= deviceLimit) will fail with a syntax/argument error instead of returning ErrDeviceLimitReached or updating, so the limit feature is broken on Postgres.

findings.title: Count-then-insert check is not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice does CountDevices, then if count >= limit calls updateDevice, otherwise does INSERT. Two concurrent requests for two different new devices can both observe count < limit and both INSERT, overshooting the limit. There is no unique-constraint/transaction guard on the count, so the limit cannot be strictly enforced under concurrency or across multiple Grafana instances.

findings.title: Anonymous auth now blocks on DB synchronously
findings.body: Authenticate was changed from fire-and-forget goroutine with background context and timeout to synchronous `TagDevice(ctx, ...)` using the request context. Every anonymous request with a cache-miss device now pays for CountDevices plus INSERT/UPDATE in the auth path, adding latency and making anonymous login availability depend on the anon_device table. A slow table or cancelled request context directly slows/fails authentication.

findings.title: Service constructor now takes db.DB instead of AnonStore
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService signature was changed from `anonStore anonstore.AnonStore` to `sqlStore db.DB` and internally calls ProvideAnonDBStore. This breaks wire DI overrides, enterprise patches, and tests that inject a fake/mock AnonStore, and removes the seam that allowed testing the service without a real DB. It should keep accepting the interface and wire the limit into the store provider instead.
